API Reference

This section contains auto-generated documentation for the core application modules.

Web Application Routes

app.execute_etl_pipeline(record_limit: int = 10) → None[source]

Asynchronous ETL Task that extracts, cleans, and loads data.

This function coordinates the full pipeline architecture: 1. Scrapes raw records using scrape.py. 2. Cleans/standardizes records using clean.py. 3. Persists records to PostgreSQL using load_data.py.

Parameters:

record_limit (int, optional) – The maximum number of new records to scrape. Defaults to 10.

Returns:

Updates the global task_status dictionary in-place.

Return type:

None

app.fetch_database_metrics() → dict[source]

Helper query runner to supply metric values to template rendering.

Returns:

A dictionary of key database metrics, aggregations, and counts.

Return type:

dict

Endpoint to inspect the background ETL process status.

Returns:

A JSON payload representing the global task_status dictionary.

Return type:

flask.Response

app.index()[source]

Main dashboard rendering route.

Returns:

Renders the index.html template with injected database metrics and task status.

Return type:

str

app.pull_data()[source]

Triggers the ETL task in a background daemon thread.

Matches form action url_for('pull_data'). Reads the desired record limit from the POST request form.

Returns:

Redirects the user back to the index page with a flash message.

Return type:

werkzeug.wrappers.Response

app.update_analysis()[source]

scrape.scrape(target_count: int = 52000, start_term_idx: int = 0, start_page: int = 1, existing_data: List[Dict[str, Any]] | None = None, seen_ids: Set[str] | None = None) → tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], Set[str], int, int][source]

Iterates through search partitions to harvest applicant entries up to a target count.

Parameters:

  • target_count (int, optional) – The total number of records to stop at. Defaults to TARGET_RECORDS.

  • start_term_idx (int, optional) – The search term index to begin with. Defaults to 0.

  • start_page (int, optional) – The GradCafe page number to begin with. Defaults to 1.

  • existing_data (list, optional) – Pre-loaded records to append to. Defaults to None.

  • seen_ids (set, optional) – Pre-loaded IDs for deduplication. Defaults to None.

Returns:

A 4-tuple containing the final lists/states: (final_data, seen_ids, term_idx, page_num).

Return type:

tuple

Data Cleaning & Normalization

clean.clean_scraped_records(raw_records: List[Dict[str, Any]]) → List[Dict[str, Any]][source]

Called by Flask (app.py) to clean and standardize raw scraped records via the LLM API.

Utilizes a ThreadPoolExecutor to process records concurrently.

Parameters:

raw_records (list) – A list of dictionaries representing uncleaned applicant records.

Returns:

A list of dictionaries representing the cleaned and standardized records.

Return type:

list

clean.worker_task(session: Session, record: Dict[str, Any]) → Tuple[bool, Dict[str, Any], str][source]

Sends a single record to the LLM endpoint for standardization.

Parameters:

  • session (requests.Session) – The active requests session.

  • record (dict) – A dictionary representing a single raw applicant record.

Returns:

A 3-tuple containing:

  • bool: True if the request was successful, False otherwise.

  • dict: The standardized record if successful, or the original record if failed.

  • str: Error message or HTTP status if the request failed, else an empty string.

Return type:

tuple

Database Ingestion

load_data.load_scraped_data_to_db(cleaned_records: List[Dict[str, Any]]) → int[source]

Parses cleaned dictionaries, maps fields to the Applicant ORM model, and commits them to the PostgreSQL database in a single transaction.

Parameters:

cleaned_records (list) – A list of dictionaries containing cleaned applicant data.

Returns:

The total number of records successfully inserted into the database.

Return type:

int

Raises:

Exception – If the database transaction fails, triggering a rollback.

query_data.run_orm_queries()[source]

Executes a suite of SQLAlchemy ORM queries to extract analytical insights from the graduate admissions database, printing formatted results to standard output.

Queries executed include:

  • Fall 2026 total applicant count.

  • Average GPA of American Fall 2026 applicants.

  • Acceptance rate for Fall 2025.

  • PhD Computer Science acceptances (original vs LLM-generated comparison).

  • Average GPA grouped by admission status.

Returns:

None
